chapters.text: 子曰：「為政以德，譬如北辰，居其所而眾星共之。」

gloss.g: the North Star (北 and 辰 appear only here)
the many stars (星 appears only here)

chapters.literal: 子曰 the Master said · 為政 governing · 以德 by virtue · 譬如 is like · 北辰 the North Star · 居 it stays in · 其所 its place · 而 and · 眾星 the many stars · 共 bow towards · 之 it
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'Governing by virtue is like the North Star: it stays in its place, and all the stars bow towards it.'
chapters.note: 共 stands for 拱 'bow towards' (gǒng). 為政 is 'to govern': 為 (wéi) is 'do, run'. The ruler who has virtue does not need to move.

chapters.text: 子曰：「《詩》三百，一言以蔽之，曰：『思無邪。』」

gloss.g: the Odes (the Book of Songs), about three hundred poems (met in 1.15)
swerving, crooked (only here)

chapters.literal: 詩三百 the Odes, three hundred · 一言 one phrase · 以 with · 蔽之 covers them · 曰 it says · 思 thought · 無邪 without swerving
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'The Odes are three hundred, and one phrase covers them all: "In thought, no swerving."'
chapters.note: 思無邪 is a line from one of the Odes, a song about horses, where 思 may be only an opening particle. Confucius reads it as 'thought'.

chapters.text: 子曰：「道之以政，齊之以刑，民免而無恥；道之以德，齊之以禮，有恥且格。」

gloss.g: come right, or reach the standard (only here)

chapters.literal: 道之 lead them · 以政 by orders · 齊之 keep them in line · 以刑 by punishments · 民 the people · 免 stay out of trouble · 而 but · 無恥 have no shame. 道之 lead them · 以德 by virtue · 齊之 keep them in line · 以禮 by ritual · 有恥 they have shame · 且 and also · 格 come right
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'Lead them by orders and keep them in line by punishments, and the people will stay out of trouble but have no sense of shame. Lead them by virtue and keep them in line by ritual, and they will have a sense of shame and come right as well.'
chapters.note: 道 stands for 導 'lead' (dǎo). 政 here is 'orders, regulations'. 格 is disputed: 'come right', 'reach the standard', or 'come to you'.

chapters.text: 子曰：「吾十有五而志于學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳順，七十而從心所欲，不踰矩。」

gloss.g: the carpenter's square, the bounds (only here)

chapters.literal: 吾 I · 十有五 at fifteen · 而 and then · 志于學 set my aim on learning. 三十 at thirty · 而立 I stood firm. 四十 at forty · 而不惑 I was not perplexed. 五十 at fifty · 而知 I knew · 天命 the decree of Heaven. 六十 at sixty · 而耳順 my ear went along. 七十 at seventy · 而從 I followed · 心所欲 what my heart wanted · 不踰 without overstepping · 矩 the square
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'At fifteen I set my aim on learning. At thirty I stood firm. At forty I was no longer perplexed. At fifty I knew the decree of Heaven. At sixty my ear went along with what it heard. At seventy I could follow what my heart wanted without overstepping the square.'
chapters.note: The first clause is a session line. 有 between numbers is 'and': 十有五 'ten and five'. 耳順 is usually read: nothing he heard jarred.

chapters.text: 孟懿子問孝。子曰：「無違。」樊遲御，子告之曰：「孟孫問孝於我，我對曰：『無違。』」樊遲曰：「何謂也？」子曰：「生，事之以禮；死，葬之以禮，祭之以禮。」

gloss.g: Meng Yizi, a noble of Lu
Fan Chi, a disciple, driving the Master's carriage
Mengsun, the same man as Meng Yizi

chapters.literal: 孟懿子 Meng Yizi · 問孝 asked about filial piety. 子曰 the Master said · 無違 do not go against. 樊遲 Fan Chi · 御 was driving · 子告之曰 the Master told him. 孟孫 Mengsun · 問孝 asked about filial piety · 於我 of me · 我對曰 I replied · 無違 do not go against. 樊遲曰 Fan Chi said · 何謂也 what did you mean? 子曰 the Master said · 生 alive · 事之 serve them · 以禮 by ritual · 死 dead · 葬之 bury them · 以禮 by ritual · 祭之 sacrifice to them · 以禮 by ritual
chapters.translation: Meng Yizi asked about filial piety. The Master said: 'Do not go against.' Fan Chi was driving him, and the Master told him: 'Mengsun asked me about filial piety, and I replied: "Do not go against."' Fan Chi said: 'What did you mean?' The Master said: 'While they are alive, serve them by ritual; when they die, bury them by ritual and sacrifice to them by ritual.'
chapters.note: 孟孫 is Meng Yizi again, by his family name. 無違 is left vague on purpose: 'do not go against' turns out to mean the rites, not the parents' wishes.

chapters.text: 孟武伯問孝。子曰：「父母唯其疾之憂。」

gloss.g: Meng Wubo, son of Meng Yizi

chapters.literal: 孟武伯 Meng Wubo · 問孝 asked about filial piety. 子曰 the Master said · 父母 father and mother · 唯 only · 其疾 his illness · 之 (object first) · 憂 worry about
chapters.translation: Meng Wubo asked about filial piety. The Master said: 'Give your father and mother nothing to worry about but your falling ill.'
chapters.note: 唯其疾之憂: the object 其疾 is put first and marked by 之, as in 4.10 義之與比. Some read it the other way: 'worry only about your parents' illness'.

chapters.text: 子游問孝。子曰：「今之孝者，是謂能養。至於犬馬，皆能有養；不敬，何以別乎？」

gloss.g: Ziyou, a disciple (met in 4.26)

chapters.literal: 子游 Ziyou · 問孝 asked about filial piety. 子曰 the Master said · 今之孝者 filial piety today · 是謂 this is called · 能養 being able to feed. 至於 when it comes to · 犬馬 dogs and horses · 皆 all · 能有養 can be fed. 不敬 without respect · 何以 by what · 別 tell them apart · 乎
chapters.translation: Ziyou asked about filial piety. The Master said: 'Filial piety today means being able to feed your parents. But even dogs and horses all get fed. Without respect, what is the difference?'
chapters.note: 能有養 is usually read 'all get fed': people feed dogs and horses too. Another reading: dogs and horses can also look after people.

chapters.text: 子夏問孝。子曰：「色難。有事，弟子服其勞；有酒食，先生饌，曾是以為孝乎？」

gloss.g: Zixia, a disciple (met in 1.7)

chapters.literal: 子夏 Zixia · 問孝 asked about filial piety. 子曰 the Master said · 色 the face · 難 is the hard part. 有事 when there is work · 弟子 the young · 服其勞 take on the toil. 有酒食 when there is wine and food · 先生 the elders · 饌 are served. 曾 really · 是以為 is this taken as · 孝 filial · 乎?
chapters.translation: Zixia asked about filial piety. The Master said: 'The face is the hard part. When there is work, the young take on the toil; when there is wine and food, the elders are served. Is that really what filial piety is?'
chapters.note: 色難 is usually read: keeping a pleasant face is the hard part. 弟子 here is 'the young' and 先生 'the elders', not 'disciples' and 'teacher'. 是以為 is 以是為 'take this as'.

chapters.text: 子曰：「吾與回言終日，不違，如愚。退而省其私，亦足以發，回也不愚。」

gloss.g: Yan Hui's personal name, which the Master uses

chapters.literal: 吾 I · 與回 with Hui · 言 talk · 終日 all day · 不違 he does not object · 如愚 as if stupid. 退 he withdraws · 而 and · 省 I examine · 其私 his private life · 亦 and yet · 足以 it is enough to · 發 bring things out. 回也 as for Hui · 不愚 he is not stupid
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'I talk with Hui all day and he never objects, as if he were stupid. But when he has withdrawn and I look at his private life, it is enough to bring out what I said. Hui is not stupid.'
chapters.note: 終日 'to the end of the day': all day. 發 is 'bring out, open up', as in 不悱不發 (session 5). The Master calls Yan Hui by his personal name 回.

chapters.text: 子曰：「視其所以，觀其所由，察其所安。人焉廋哉？人焉廋哉？」
chapters.literal: 視 look at · 其所以 the means he uses · 觀 observe · 其所由 the path he takes · 察 inspect · 其所安 what he is at ease in. 人 a person · 焉 how · 廋 hide · 哉? 人焉廋哉 how can a person hide?
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'Look at the means he uses, observe the path he takes, inspect what he is at ease in. How can a person hide? How can a person hide?'
chapters.note: 所以, 所由 and 所安 are all 'that which': what he uses, what he follows, what he rests in. 焉 is 'how?', as in 4.1.

chapters.text: 子曰：「溫故而知新，可以為師矣。」
chapters.literal: 溫故 review the old · 而 and · 知新 know the new · 可以 can · 為師 be a teacher · 矣
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'Review the old and come to know the new, and you can be a teacher.'
chapters.note: A session line.

chapters.text: 子曰：「君子不器。」
chapters.literal: 君子 the gentleman · 不器 is not a vessel
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'The gentleman is not a vessel.'
chapters.note: A session line. A vessel has one use; the gentleman is not limited to one.

chapters.text: 子貢問君子。子曰：「先行其言而後從之。」

gloss.g: Zigong, a disciple (met in 1.10)

chapters.literal: 子貢 Zigong · 問君子 asked about the gentleman. 子曰 the Master said · 先 first · 行其言 he puts his words into practice · 而後 and only then · 從之 [the words] follow it
chapters.translation: Zigong asked about the gentleman. The Master said: 'He first puts his words into practice, and only then lets them follow.'
chapters.note: Also punctuated 先行，其言而後從之: 'he acts first, and his words follow after'. Either way, action comes before talk.

chapters.text: 子曰：「君子周而不比，小人比而不周。」
chapters.literal: 君子 the gentleman · 周 is open to all · 而 and · 不比 takes no sides. 小人 the small man · 比 takes sides · 而 and · 不周 is not open to all
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'The gentleman is open to all and does not take sides; the small man takes sides and is not open to all.'
chapters.note: 比 is read bì: 'side with, form a clique', as in 4.10.

chapters.text: 子曰：「學而不思則罔，思而不學則殆。」
chapters.literal: 學而不思 learn and not think · 則罔 then lost · 思而不學 think and not learn · 則殆 then in danger
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'Learning without thinking leaves you lost; thinking without learning leaves you in danger.'
chapters.note: A session line.

chapters.text: 子曰：「攻乎異端，斯害也已。」
chapters.literal: 攻 working at · 乎 on · 異端 strange doctrines · 斯 this · 害 is harmful · 也已 indeed
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'Working on strange doctrines does nothing but harm.'
chapters.note: Much disputed. 攻 is 'attack' or 'work at'; 已 is 'stop' or a final particle. So also: 'Attack the strange doctrines, and the harm will stop.'

chapters.text: 子曰：「由！誨女知之乎！知之為知之，不知為不知，是知也。」

gloss.g: Zilu's personal name, which the Master uses

chapters.literal: 由 You (Zilu)! · 誨女 shall I teach you · 知之 knowing · 乎! 知之 knowing it · 為知之 count as knowing it · 不知 not knowing · 為不知 count as not knowing · 是 this · 知也 is knowing
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'You (Zilu)! Shall I teach you what knowing is? When you know a thing, hold that you know it; when you do not know it, hold that you do not. That is knowing.'
chapters.note: The second half is a session line. 女 stands for 汝 'you'. 由 is Zilu, the bold disciple the Master often reins in.

chapters.text: 子張學干祿。子曰：「多聞闕疑，慎言其餘，則寡尤；多見闕殆，慎行其餘，則寡悔。言寡尤，行寡悔，祿在其中矣。」

gloss.g: Zizhang, a disciple

chapters.literal: 子張 Zizhang · 學 was studying · 干祿 going after a salary. 子曰 the Master said · 多聞 hear much · 闕疑 leave aside the doubtful · 慎言 speak carefully · 其餘 of the rest · 則 then · 寡尤 little blame. 多見 see much · 闕殆 leave aside the risky · 慎行 act carefully · 其餘 on the rest · 則 then · 寡悔 few regrets. 言寡尤 words with little blame · 行寡悔 actions with few regrets · 祿 the salary · 在其中 is in that · 矣
chapters.translation: Zizhang was studying how to win an official's salary. The Master said: 'Hear much, leave aside what is doubtful, and speak carefully about the rest: then you will incur little blame. See much, leave aside what is risky, and act carefully on the rest: then you will have few regrets. With little blame for your words and few regrets for your actions, the salary is already in it.'
chapters.note: 干 is 'go after', 祿 an official's pay. 殆 here is 'risky, unsure', not 'in danger' as in 2.15.

chapters.text: 哀公問曰：「何為則民服？」孔子對曰：「舉直錯諸枉，則民服；舉枉錯諸直，則民不服。」

gloss.g: Duke Ai, ruler of Lu
Confucius, as the narrator names him before a ruler

chapters.literal: 哀公 Duke Ai · 問曰 asked · 何為 doing what · 則 then · 民服 the people submit? 孔子 Confucius · 對曰 replied · 舉直 raise the straight · 錯諸枉 set them over the crooked · 則 then · 民服 the people submit. 舉枉 raise the crooked · 錯諸直 set them over the straight · 則 then · 民不服 the people do not submit
chapters.translation: Duke Ai asked: 'What should I do to make the people submit?' Confucius replied: 'Raise up the straight and set them over the crooked, and the people will submit. Raise up the crooked and set them over the straight, and the people will not submit.'
chapters.note: When a ruler asks, the narrator writes 孔子 and 對曰 'replied', not 子曰. 錯 stands for 措 'put'; 諸 is 之於 'them over'.

chapters.text: 季康子問：「使民敬、忠以勸，如之何？」子曰：「臨之以莊，則敬；孝慈，則忠；舉善而教不能，則勸。」

gloss.g: Ji Kangzi, head of the Ji clan, the real power in Lu
kind to the young (only here)

chapters.literal: 季康子 Ji Kangzi · 問 asked · 使民 to make the people · 敬 respectful · 忠 loyal · 以勸 and eager · 如之何 what should I do? 子曰 the Master said · 臨之 face them · 以莊 with dignity · 則敬 then they are respectful. 孝慈 be filial and kind · 則忠 then they are loyal. 舉善 raise the good · 而教 and instruct · 不能 those not able · 則勸 then they are eager
chapters.translation: Ji Kangzi asked: 'How can I make the people respectful and loyal, and eager to do their best?' The Master said: 'Face them with dignity, and they will be respectful. Be filial and kind, and they will be loyal. Raise up the good and instruct those who are not able, and they will be eager.'
chapters.note: 孝慈: filial to your own parents, kind to the young. 以 here is 'and', joining 忠 and 勸.

chapters.text: 或謂孔子曰：「子奚不為政？」子曰：「《書》云：『孝乎惟孝，友于兄弟，施於有政。』是亦為政，奚其為為政？」

gloss.g: the Documents (the Book of Documents)
only, the same word as 唯 (only here)

chapters.literal: 或 someone · 謂孔子曰 said to Confucius · 子 you · 奚 why · 不為政 do not take part in government? 子曰 the Master said · 書云 the Documents say · 孝乎 filial! · 惟孝 only filial · 友于兄弟 a friend to your brothers · 施於 it extends to · 有政 the government. 是 this · 亦 too · 為政 is taking part in government · 奚其 why then · 為 must one do · 為政 government?
chapters.translation: Someone said to Confucius: 'Why do you not take part in government?' The Master said: 'The Documents say: "Be filial, only filial, and a friend to your brothers, and it will reach the government." This too is taking part in government. Why must taking part mean holding office?'
chapters.note: 子 here is 'you', a polite address, not 'the Master'. 為政 is used two ways: 'take part in government' and, at the end, 'hold office'. 于 is 於.

chapters.text: 子曰：「人而無信，不知其可也。大車無輗，小車無軏，其何以行之哉？」

gloss.g: the pin joining an ox cart's shaft to its yoke (only here)
the same pin on a horse carriage (only here)

chapters.literal: 人 a person · 而 and yet · 無信 not trustworthy · 不知 I do not know · 其可 what he is good for · 也. 大車 a big ox cart · 無輗 with no yoke pin · 小車 a small carriage · 無軏 with no yoke pin · 其 then · 何以 by what · 行之 make it go · 哉?
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'A person who is not trustworthy: I do not know what he is good for. A big cart with no yoke pin, a small carriage with no yoke pin: how could you make them go?'
chapters.note: 信, keeping one's word, is the pin that joins a person to others. 而 between a subject and its verb is 'and yet, if'.

chapters.text: 子張問：「十世可知也？」子曰：「殷因於夏禮，所損益，可知也；周因於殷禮，所損益，可知也。其或繼周者，雖百世可知也。」

gloss.g: the Shang dynasty, before Zhou
the Xia dynasty, before Yin
the Zhou dynasty, Confucius's own

chapters.literal: 子張問 Zizhang asked · 十世 ten generations on · 可知也 can it be known? 子曰 the Master said · 殷 Yin · 因於 built on · 夏禮 the rites of Xia · 所損益 what it took away and added · 可知也 can be known. 周 Zhou · 因於 built on · 殷禮 the rites of Yin · 所損益 what it took away and added · 可知也 can be known. 其或 if perhaps · 繼周者 someone continues Zhou · 雖 even · 百世 a hundred generations on · 可知也 can be known
chapters.translation: Zizhang asked: 'Can ten generations from now be known?' The Master said: 'Yin built on the rites of Xia, and what it took away and added can be known. Zhou built on the rites of Yin, and what it took away and added can be known. If someone continues Zhou, even a hundred generations from now can be known.'
chapters.note: Xia, Yin (Shang) and Zhou are the three dynasties. In 十世可知也, 也 stands for 邪 (yé) and makes it a question. 因 is 'build on, follow'.

chapters.text: 子曰：「非其鬼而祭之，諂也。見義不為，無勇也。」
chapters.literal: 非 not · 其鬼 his own spirits · 而 and yet · 祭之 sacrifice to them · 諂 flattery · 也. 見義 see what is right · 不為 not do it · 無勇 lacking courage · 也
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'To sacrifice to spirits that are not your own is flattery. To see what is right and not do it is to lack courage.'
chapters.note: 鬼 here are ancestral spirits: a family sacrifices to its own. 諂 'flattery' is the word from 1.15.
